decision.applicability_reason: Project metadata marks this a federal-aid contract funded under Title 23, so FHWA-1273 incorporation applies.
decision.explanation: Project metadata confirms this is a federal-aid contract funded under Title 23, making FHWA-1273 physical incorporation mandatory. Searching the entire reviewed package — Addendum_A.pdf, General_Conditions.pdf, Proposal_and_General_Notices.pdf, and Special_Provisions.pdf — reveals no physical inclusion of FHWA-1273, nor any clause that references or incorporates it. Moreover, the Proposal_and_General_Notices.pdf affirmatively states 'Federal aid No' and 'Buy America/BABA applicable No' at lines Proposal_and_General_Notices.pdf|p1|L6 and L7, which directly conflicts with the project metadata establishing federal-aid applicability. No Addendum revises this provision. The form is entirely absent from the package, and the proposal summary affirmatively misrepresents the federal-aid status. This is a material deviation from the Challenge Reference Rule requiring physical incorporation.
decision.recommended_action: Human review required: FHWA-1273 is not physically incorporated anywhere in the contract package, and the proposal summary incorrectly states 'Federal aid No' contrary to project metadata. Confirm federal-aid status and ensure FHWA-1273 is physically inserted into the package before execution.

criteria.challenge_reference_rule: If federal-aid metadata makes FHWA-1273 applicable, the form must be physically included in the package; a reference-only statement is insufficient for challenge scoring.
criteria.review_expectation: Flag a covered contract that only references FHWA-1273 instead of physically including the form.

decision.applicability_reason: DelDOT bid package governed by Section 102.8 proposal-guaranty requirements.
decision.explanation: The governing document (Proposal_and_General_Notices.pdf) states the bid security must 'total one-tenth (10%) of the bid amount.' One-tenth (10%) of the bid amount is substantively identical to 10% of the total bid price required by the Challenge Reference Rule. The phrasing 'one-tenth (10%)' and 'bid amount' versus 'total bid price' is a restatement in different words that preserves the same obligation and percentage. No Addendum revises this provision. The clause is fully compliant with the reference requirement.
decision.recommended_action: No action required — the proposal guaranty clause in Proposal_and_General_Notices.pdf satisfies the 10% requirement. Human reviewer should confirm the physical bid bond instrument accompanying the proposal is present and equals 10% of the submitted bid price.

decision.applicability_reason: Successful-bidder execution package governed by Section 103.7.
decision.explanation: The governing clause in General_Conditions.pdf (the highest-precedence document addressing this provision) states that the successful bidder shall return required execution documents 'within the reference period' and 'furnish required proof of insurance.' The phrase 'within the reference period' defers to the governing reference rather than restating or contradicting the 20-calendar-day deadline, and 'furnish required proof of insurance' preserves the insurance-before-execution obligation without negating or altering it. Under the operating rules, a clause that defers to the reference instead of repeating its figures is compliant — a missing number is not an omission when the clause contradicts nothing. No Addendum revises this provision. The clause is therefore consistent with the Challenge Reference Rule and does not constitute a material deviation.
decision.recommended_action: No action required on this provision. Human reviewer should confirm that the phrase 'reference period' is understood by all parties to mean 20 calendar days after notice of award as specified in DelDOT 103.7, and that the insurance-before-execution sequence is enforced in practice.

decision.explanation: The governing document (Proposal_and_General_Notices.pdf) affirmatively states that 'later issued Addenda may be disregarded.' This directly conflicts with the Challenge Reference Rule, which requires the package to acknowledge the current (latest) addenda and prohibits treating the original proposal as self-updating. The project metadata confirms that Addendum_A has been issued, making this requirement applicable. No subsequent Addendum revises this specific provision — Addendum_A addresses bonds and licenses, not addenda acknowledgment currency. The clause therefore stands as a material deviation: it explicitly permits ignoring later-issued addenda, which is the exact conduct the reference rule prohibits.
decision.recommended_action: Human review required. The addenda acknowledgment clause in Proposal_and_General_Notices.pdf expressly permits disregarding later-issued addenda, directly contradicting the requirement to acknowledge and apply the latest addendum (Addendum_A). The clause should be revised to require acknowledgment of all issued addenda, including Addendum_A, before the package is accepted.

decision.applicability_reason: Multiple contract documents are incorporated and may conflict, so DelDOT 105.6 applies.
decision.explanation: The General Conditions clause at lines L12–L13 instructs that all contract documents be read together (complementary treatment) and that conflicts be resolved by applying 'the same priority sequence listed in the applicable contract documents.' This is a deferral to the governing reference rather than a restatement of the specific hierarchy. Under the operating rules, a clause that defers to the reference rather than repeating its figures or sequence is compliant — a missing enumeration is not an omission when the clause contradicts nothing and points back to the applicable contract documents. The clause does not invert, omit, or negate any tier of the DelDOT 105.6 hierarchy; it preserves the obligation by incorporation by reference. No Addendum revises this provision. The finding is NO_FLAG.
decision.recommended_action: No action required. Confirm that the project's applicable contract documents (e.g., Standard Specifications) contain the full DelDOT 105.6 hierarchy so the deferral clause has a complete sequence to point to.

decision.applicability_reason: Package includes change-notification requirements under DelDOT 104.3.
decision.explanation: The governing clause in General_Conditions.pdf (lines L17–L19) states that alleged changes require 'timely written notice and the reference follow-up documentation within the stated period.' It does not affirmatively conflict with the Challenge Reference Rule: it does not shorten or extend the 7-calendar-day deadline, does not make notice optional, does not permit oral direction alone to modify scope/price/time (that is separately addressed at L14–L16), and does not negate any required step. decision.applicability_reason: Contract and subcontract performance records are subject to the Right to Audit notice.
decision.explanation: The package text deviates from the reference in two material respects. First, it limits audit scope to 'only prime-contractor records,' expressly excluding subcontractor records, whereas the reference requires both prime-contractor and subcontractor records to be available for audit. Second, it shortens the retention period from three years (as required) to one (1) year after final payment. No Addendum revises this provision; Addendum_A addresses only bonds and licenses. The governing document (Proposal_and_General_Notices.pdf) therefore contains affirmative conflicts on both scope and duration. Both deviations are provable by direct quotation of the package text.
decision.recommended_action: Review and correct the Right to Audit clause to (1) extend audit scope to include subcontractor records and (2) restore the retention period to three years after final payment, consistent with the reference requirement.

decision.applicability_reason: Project metadata indicates subcontractors will be used, so DelDOT 108.1 subletting limits apply.
decision.explanation: After reviewing every file in the package — General_Conditions.pdf, Addendum_A.pdf, Proposal_and_General_Notices.pdf, and Special_Provisions.pdf — no clause addresses contract subletting. There is no provision establishing the 50% self-performance floor, no written-consent requirement for subletting, and no statement that the prime retains full contract responsibility when work is sublet. The governing document (General_Conditions.pdf) covers bonds, insurance, document coordination, contract changes, and change notification, but is silent on subletting. Addendum_A revises only bonds and licenses. The requirement is entirely absent from the package. Because subcontracting is planned (metadata: subcontracting_planned = true) and the requirement is marked applicable, this complete omission is a material deviation from DelDOT 108.1. Human review is required to determine whether the provision must be added before contract execution.
decision.recommended_action: Review required — the contract subletting clause (50% self-performance minimum, written consent for subletting, prime retains responsibility) is absent from the package. Confirm whether it appears in an unproduced document (e.g., Standard Specifications incorporated by reference) or must be added as a special provision before execution.

criteria.challenge_reference_rule: When subcontracting applies, use DelDOT Section 108.1 as the challenge baseline: the prime performs no less than 50% of the total original contract price with its own organization, excluding designated specialty items as provided by the reference; subletting requires written consent and does not relieve the prime of contract responsibility.
criteria.review_expectation: Verify self-performance, approval, licensing, and flow-down requirements are not materially weakened.
